chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of the Husayniyyun, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
That the chard suppresses the vein of leprosy, and what enters the inside of the vitiligo sufferer is like the leaf of the chard.

key_terms.السِّلْق: Chard, a type of leafy green vegetable known for medicinal uses

ai.seo_question: What are the medicinal benefits of chard according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) highlights the therapeutic efficacy of chard (*silq*) in treating dermatological conditions, specifically noting its ability to suppress the 'vein of leprosy' (*'irq al-judham*) and its effectiveness for vitiligo (*al-barsam*) when ingested or applied. This narration reflects the broader Shia tradition of *al-Tibb al-Nabawi* and *al-Tibb al-A'imma*, where natural remedies are viewed as divine signs (*ayat*) and practical means (*asbab*) for healing, bridging spiritual well-being with physical health.
